title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 3: love shows who receive glory — not foresight-cause of the decree
pass_a_gloss: Those words, for them that love him, show us of what sort finally all those are for whom from eternity he prepared glory: but they do not indicate that this love foreseen was the cause or reason why glory was destined to them. The same love of God which destined them freely unto glory also destined them unto this love of God, by which, being driven, they enter the way that rightly leads unto glory. Our love of God therefore is an effect of the Divine love by which he elected and predestinated us unto salvation, and therefore it is foolishly supposed as the cause of our election. Hither look those words of the Apostle, We love God because he first loved us. 1 John iv. 19.
pass_b_english: Reply: "for those who love him" tells what sort of people finally receive the glory he prepared from eternity — it does not make foresight of that love the cause why glory was destined to them. The same love that freely destined them to glory also destined them to love God, and by that love they take the road that leads to glory. So our love of God is an effect of the divine love that elected and predestined us to salvation — foolishly taken as election's cause. So the Apostle: "We love God because he first loved us" (1 John 4:19).
source_text: Verba illa, iis qui diligunt eum, ostendunt nobis quales tandem illi omnes sint, quibus ab aeterno gloriam praeparavit: sed non indicant hanc dilectionem praevisam fuisse causam aut rationem cur gloria fuit illis destinata. Idem amor Dei qui eos destinavit gratuito ad gloriam, destinavit etiam eos ad hanc dilectionem Dei, qua impellente viam ineunt quae recte ducit ad gloriam. Est itaque nostra Dei dilectio effectum amoris Divini quo nos elegit & praedestinavit ad salutem, atque idcirco inepte supponitur causa nostrae electionis. Huc spectant illa Apostoli verba, Nos diligimus Deum quia ipse prior dilexit nos. 1 Joan. iv. 19.
